correctness.rationale: Independently checked the moving-switch derivative. Write A_r(t)=∫_0^t exp(-rv)dv, U=T-h, z=C_0 exp(-bτ)+qA_b(τ) and w=exp(-ah)z+qA_a(h) for the start and end concentrations. Translation of both switches gives J'=(a-b){z[A_a(h)+exp(-ah)A_b(U-τ)]-wA_b(U-τ)}=(a-b)A_a(h)[z-qA_b(U-τ)]. The leading factor is exactly the strictly positive G in the result, even when b=0. For b>0 and E=q/b, C_0≥E makes J' strictly positive, and C_0<E makes it strictly increasing and positive at U. Its sign at zero is the sign of C_0-E(1-exp(-bU)), with equality giving the unique boundary minimum. The interior zero gives the stated logarithm. For b=0 the derivative is affine with slope 2Gq>0, giving the clipped formula. At an interior optimum with b>0 the derivative is 2Gk sinh[b(τ-τ_*)]; integrating it, and integrating the appropriate derivative on the boundary and for b=0, verifies all four regret cases. An independent segment calculation gave 2.578509392222384 and 2.196190111820411 for the canonical immediate and optimal exposures. evidence: Record f81123358ad7 gives the positive adult mortality, constant-emergence limit in RESULT.md lines 21–25 and 74–78. Set its formal immature loss to zero, adult loss to the air baseline b, recruitment to the air source q, initial adults to C_0, horizon to U, and fractional impulse removal to G. The pulse reduction of its burden is G z(τ)A_b(U-τ), whose negative derivative is exactly J'(τ). Thus for b>0 the entire air-window ranking, threshold and regrets coincide with that impulse's up to a τ-independent constant. The b=0 case follows by continuity of this reduction, though the cohort statement assumes positive mortality. Record 0031cd3b8d1b also has this impulse product on a shifted time interval when outdoor and indoor decay rates are equal; its stated unshifted scope has zero initial indoor concentration and positive outdoor concentration.

value.rationale: Under a genuine operating constraint (one contiguous fixed-runtime episode), the exact cancellation of the enhanced rate from all timing comparisons is a useful model benchmark. The result quantifies how much, not just which way, mistiming hurts; the finite interval has exactly the time-ordering and regret of the calibrated instantaneous proxy despite its continuing emissions and two switches. This does not assert optimality for split schedules, physical safety, or HVAC performance outside the well-mixed constant-source model.
